story_description: Users launching Blaze for the first time need guided onboarding that detects installed AI CLIs, offers one-click installation for missing ones, and configures the environment automatically so they can start coding immediately.
task_description: Implement the Plugins Recommendations Screen that displays plugin recommendations grouped by CLI, dynamically filtering to only show sections for installed CLIs, with plugin cards containing install buttons for each recommended extension.
atom: Plugins Recommendations Screen with Dynamic CLI-Based Filtering
atom_description: A SwiftUI view that presents plugin recommendations organized by CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Aider), dynamically showing only sections for CLIs the user has installed. Each plugin is displayed as a card with name, description, install button, and status indicator. Installation triggers the appropriate package manager or opens external links for manual setup.
problem_statement: Users who have just installed AI CLIs may not know about useful plugins and extensions that enhance their workflow. Without guidance, they miss productivity improvements from tools like Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, Braintrust for Claude Code, or official extension catalogs for Gemini CLI. The onboarding flow should surface these recommendations contextually based on which CLIs the user has installed.
scope_in: Display plugin recommendations grouped by installed CLI only
Show Claude Code plugins section when Claude Code is installed: Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, Braintrust
Show Gemini CLI section when Gemini CLI is installed: link to official extensions catalog
Show Codex CLI section when Codex CLI is installed: MCP servers info, AGENTS.md guide link
Show Aider section when Aider is installed: Git integration tips card
Render each plugin as a card with icon, name, description, and install/view action button
Track installation status per plugin (not installed, installing, installed)
Handle plugin installation via npm, pip, brew, or external URL opening
Persist plugin installation choices for session continuity
Provide Skip button to bypass plugin installation entirely
Provide Next button to proceed after reviewing recommendations
scope_out: Plugin configuration or settings after installation - deferred to CLI-specific settings
Auto-updating plugins to newer versions - manual process
Custom plugin discovery from registries - only curated recommendations shown
Plugin uninstallation from this screen - handled elsewhere if needed
Plugin compatibility validation - assume latest versions work
Cross-CLI plugin sharing or dependencies - each CLI section is independent
assumptions: User has completed CLI detection screen and OnboardingState contains installed CLI list
Plugin installation commands are stable and documented by plugin maintainers
External URLs for catalogs and guides are accessible and maintained
npm and pip are available in PATH after dependency installation in CLI detection screen
User has internet connectivity for plugin downloads and external links
constraints: Must only show plugin sections for CLIs confirmed installed in OnboardingState
Must not block UI during plugin installation - use async with progress feedback
Must handle offline gracefully - show plugins but disable install buttons with offline message
Plugin cards must be accessible with VoiceOver including install button state
Must complete render within 500ms regardless of number of plugins shown
External link opening must use NSWorkspace.shared.open for security
functional_requirements: FR1: On view appear, read installed CLIs from OnboardingState and filter plugin sections to only show relevant ones
FR2: Display Claude Code Plugins section with Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, and Braintrust cards when Claude Code is installed
FR3: Display Gemini CLI Extensions section with official catalog link card when Gemini CLI is installed
FR4: Display Codex CLI section with MCP servers card and AGENTS.md guide card when Codex CLI is installed
FR5: Display Aider section with Git integration tips card when Aider is installed
FR6: Each plugin card shows icon, name, brief description, and contextual action button
FR7: Action button for npm/pip installable plugins triggers installation with progress indicator
FR8: Action button for external links opens URL in default browser via NSWorkspace
FR9: Track installation status per plugin and update card UI to show Installed checkmark on success
FR10: Skip button navigates to next onboarding screen without installing any plugins
FR11: Next button navigates to next screen after user has reviewed recommendations
FR12: Show empty state with encouraging message if no CLIs are installed (edge case fallback)
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Initial render completes within 500ms with smooth animations for section reveals
NFR2: Plugin installation feedback updates UI within 200ms of state change
NFR3: Support VoiceOver with meaningful labels for all interactive elements
NFR4: Respect system Reduce Motion preference for section reveal animations
NFR5: Memory footprint stays under 20MB for plugin recommendation data structures
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create PluginsRecommendationsView.swift with @StateObject for PluginsRecommendationsViewModel
Step 2: Define PluginRecommendation struct with id, name, description, iconName, cliType, installType enum (npm, pip, brew, externalUrl), installCommand or url, and isInstalled
Step 3: Define PluginInstallType enum with cases: npmGlobal, pipInstall, brewInstall, externalUrl
Step 4: Define SupportedCLI extension or use existing enum to associate plugins with each CLI
Step 5: Create PluginsRecommendationsViewModel with Published properties: installedCLIs, pluginsBySection, installationStates
Step 6: Implement loadRecommendations method that reads OnboardingState.installedCLIs and builds filtered plugin list
Step 7: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Claude Code: Gastown (npm), Continuous-Claude-v2 (npm), Braintrust (npm)
Step 8: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Gemini CLI: Official Extensions Catalog (externalUrl)
Step 9: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Codex CLI: MCP Servers Guide (externalUrl), AGENTS.md Guide (externalUrl)
Step 10: Create hardcoded plugin definitions for Aider: Git Integration Tips (externalUrl)
Step 11: Implement installPlugin async method that dispatches to appropriate installer based on PluginInstallType
Step 12: Create npmInstall helper that runs npm install -g packageName with progress tracking
Step 13: Create openExternalUrl helper that uses NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)
Step 14: Build PluginSectionView subview that renders section header and list of PluginCardView items
Step 15: Build PluginCardView subview with icon, name, description, and action button (Install or Open)
Step 16: Implement action button states: default (Install/Open), installing (spinner), installed (checkmark), error (retry)
Step 17: Add section reveal animation using withAnimation and staggered delays when motion is enabled
Step 18: Build empty state view shown when installedCLIs is empty with message to go back and install a CLI
Step 19: Wire up Skip button to call coordinator.navigateNext without installing anything
Step 20: Wire up Next button to call coordinator.navigateNext after logging selected plugins
Step 21: Add telemetry events for screen view, plugin install attempts, and navigation actions
Step 22: Write unit tests for PluginsRecommendationsViewModel filtering logic
Step 23: Write unit tests for plugin install method dispatch based on install type
Step 24: Write UI tests for section visibility based on mocked installedCLIs state
data_model_changes: Add PluginRecommendation struct with fields: id (String), name (String), description (String), iconSystemName (String), cliType (SupportedCLI), installType (PluginInstallType), installCommand (String?), externalUrl (URL?), isRecommended (Bool)
Add PluginInstallType enum with cases: npmGlobal, pipInstall, brewInstall, externalUrl
Add PluginInstallState enum with cases: notInstalled, installing, installed, failed(Error)
Add OnboardingState.selectedPlugins: [String] to persist user choices across sessions
api_contracts: PluginInstaller.npmInstall(package: String, progressHandler: (Double) -> Void) async throws -> Void
event_contracts: OnboardingEvent.pluginsScreenViewed(installedCLIs: [SupportedCLI], sectionsShown: [String]) - emitted when screen appears with context
OnboardingEvent.pluginInstallStarted(pluginId: String, pluginName: String, installType: PluginInstallType) - emitted when install begins
OnboardingEvent.pluginInstallCompleted(pluginId: String, pluginName: String, success: Bool, error: String?) - emitted when install finishes
OnboardingEvent.pluginExternalLinkOpened(pluginId: String, url: String) - emitted when external link is opened
OnboardingEvent.pluginsScreenSkipped - emitted when user clicks Skip
OnboardingEvent.pluginsScreenCompleted(installedPlugins: [String], viewedPlugins: [String]) - emitted when user clicks Next
ui_states: Loading state: Brief skeleton placeholders while filtering plugin sections (under 200ms)
Populated state: Sections for each installed CLI with plugin cards rendered
Empty state: Message indicating no CLIs installed with Back button to return to CLI detection
Installing state: Individual plugin card shows spinner during installation
Installed state: Plugin card shows green checkmark and Installed label
Error state: Plugin card shows red indicator with error message and Retry button
ui_interactions: Tap Install button on plugin card to trigger npm/pip/brew installation flow
Tap Open button on external link plugin card to open URL in browser
Tap Retry button on failed installation to re-attempt installation
Tap Skip button to proceed without installing any plugins
Tap Next button to proceed after reviewing and optionally installing plugins
Tap Back button to return to previous onboarding screen
Scroll vertically to view all plugin sections when content exceeds viewport
ui_copy: Enhance your AI coding workflow with these plugins
Gastown - Advanced prompt templates and session management
Continuous-Claude-v2 - Automatic session continuity and memory
Braintrust - Evaluation and observability for AI coding
View Official Catalog - Browse Google's extension marketplace
MCP Servers Guide - Model Context Protocol server setup

Install at least one CLI to see plugin recommendations
edge_cases: User has no CLIs installed - show empty state with Back button instead of empty sections
All plugin installs fail - allow proceeding with warning toast about partial setup
Network unavailable during npm install - detect offline and show offline-specific error message
Plugin already globally installed from previous session - detect via npm list -g and show as Installed
External URL returns 404 - cannot pre-validate, user sees browser error (acceptable)
User rapidly taps Install on multiple plugins - queue installations to run sequentially
Plugin npm package name changed - installation fails, show error with link to manual instructions
failure_modes: npm install fails due to permission denied - prompt user to fix npm permissions or use sudo (with warning)
External URL open fails silently - log error but show success since browser opened
Plugin version incompatible with installed CLI version - defer to plugin maintainer docs, not our problem
Memory pressure during multiple installs - let system handle, our footprint is minimal
Onboarding state corrupt and installedCLIs empty - treat as no CLIs, show empty state
rollback_plan: Plugin installations can be rolled back via npm uninstall -g packageName or pip uninstall packageName. External link opens have no rollback needed. If this screen causes issues, it can be temporarily disabled in OnboardingCoordinator by skipping directly to next screen. User selections stored in OnboardingState can be cleared via UserDefaults.removeObject.

dependencies: Requires OnboardingState with installedCLIs populated from CLI detection screen. Requires OnboardingCoordinator for navigation. Uses npm from PATH (installed in CLI detection screen). Can be developed with mock OnboardingState for isolated testing.
status_reason: Specified and ready for implementation. Depends on CLI detection screen (T004) for installedCLIs data but can be developed in parallel with mocked state. Low risk due to straightforward UI with minimal system interactions.

risks: npm install may fail if user npm configuration is broken or permissions are wrong
External URLs may become stale if plugin maintainers change documentation locations
Plugin package names may change causing install commands to fail
User may not have network connectivity during plugin installation attempts
mitigations: Detect npm errors and show clear error message with link to manual installation instructions
Use stable URLs from official documentation and check quarterly for link rot
Pin specific known-good package names and version ranges in plugin definitions
Detect network status before install attempt and show offline state with message to retry later
risk_register.blast_radius: Affects only Onboarding module and new plugin-related files. Does not modify existing session, engine, or settings code. Plugin installation affects user global npm packages which is expected and reversible.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If plugin installation proves unreliable, convert all Install buttons to Open buttons that link to plugin documentation for manual installation. Screen remains useful as a curated recommendation list even without automated installation.

persistence: OnboardingState.installedCLIs: [SupportedCLI] read from UserDefaults (set by CLI detection screen)
